ingredients.item: fresh mussels, scrubbed, beards removed, closed
ingredients.preparation: tap-test any gapers: a live one closes; an open non-closer is discarded

ingredients.item: garlic , sliced thin, not grated — slices toast sweet
scallions , sliced, whites and greens separated
gochujang , optional but this record's signature
Crusty bread or steamed rice , lemon wedges, an empty bowl for shells at the table's center

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Mussels into the warm pan with the toasted base and a splash of mirin, lid on, high heat under now — they steam in their own liquor, 3–5 minutes, one hard shake at the halfway mark.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the shells spring open and the kitchen smells of garlic steam and ocean. Off the heat the moment the majority gape; a mussel that refused its colleagues gets one more minute in the residual steam and then, still shut, goes to the discard bowl — the unopened mussel is the one absolute no in shellfish.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Gochujang and sesame oil in, swirled through the liquor off the heat until the pot runs glossy orange-gold; scallion greens over.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the broth test with the eating spoon: briny, buttery, garlic-sweet, a warm gochujang hum behind — it should taste like the sea made a sauce. Flat? A squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt; this pot is forgiving.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Pan to the table on its trivet, shells bowl beside, bread or rice armed. The eating: pull the mussels from the shells by hand or with an empty shell as tongs (the tradition's own tool), a mussel and a spoon of broth per bite, bread for the pot's floor.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the empty-pot test: no broth left, the bread has been torn to ragged edges, someone has asked what was in the sauce. That is the record finished properly.

storageNotes: Live mussels keep 1–2 days on ice in the fridge in an open bowl (never sealed — they breathe). Cooked, 1 day, meat picked for pasta or rice; the strained broth is the next day's soup base.
Variations: the oyster sauce (#SF12's butter-gochujang build) transplants whole; clams run the same pot at a shorter clock (#SF15); a splash of soju in the steam for the tent's version.
